summary: FalkorDB is a Redis-module graph database (openCypher, SSPLv1) that speaks the Redis protocol on port 6379 and ships a bundled graph-visualization Browser UI on port 3000. For the hackathon the single most important finding is that **Docker is NOT installed on this Mac** (verified: `which docker` → not found, no brew either), and there is a fully working Docker-free path: `pip install falkordblite`, an embedded build that bundles Redis+the FalkorDB module into a subprocess your Python process owns. I installed it (falkordblite==0.10.0) and verified live on this box: node/edge creation, a 3-hop variable-length Cypher traversal, path objects, parameterized queries, HNSW vector index creation + `db.idx.vector.queryNodes` KNN search, and cross-session persistence to a file. I also proved that FalkorDBLite can be forced to bind a real TCP port (`serverconfig={'port':'6399','bind':'127.0.0.1'}`), after which the *standard* `falkordb` PyPI client (v1.6.2) — and by extension the `falkordb` npm client and the Browser UI — connects to it over TCP, so Lite is a genuine drop-in for the Docker server, not just a toy. Cloud has a real FREE tier at app.falkordb.cloud (no TLS/backups/HA, but multi-graph + access control), and GraphRAG-SDK (`pip install graphrag-sdk[litellm]`) sits on top for LLM-driven ontology extraction and natural-language Q&A over the graph.
setup_steps: DECISION: pick ONE of three paths. (A) Docker server — best if any teammate's laptop has Docker Desktop, gives you the Browser UI for free. (B) FalkorDBLite — zero Docker, zero sudo, works on THIS Mac today, verified. (C) FalkorDB Cloud free tier — best if 3 humans + agents on different machines need to share ONE graph. For a 3-person hackathon team I recommend C as the shared source of truth + B on each laptop for fast local iteration.

PATH A (Docker, gives Browser UI): `docker run -p 6379:6379 -p 3000:3000 -it --rm -v $(pwd)/falkordb-data:/var/lib/falkordb/data falkordb/falkordb:latest`  — then open http://localhost:3000 for the graph visualizer. Omit the -v and you LOSE all data when the container stops (--rm).
PATH B step 1 (verified on this Mac): FalkorDBLite needs Python >= 3.12. The system python3 here is older, so create a venv: `uv venv .venv --python 3.12`
PATH B step 2: `uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python falkordblite falkordb`  (falkordblite==0.10.0 for the embedded server; falkordb==1.6.2 is the normal client, useful for the TCP mode below)

PATH B step 3: import is NOT `import falkordblite` — it is `from redislite.falkordb_client import FalkorDB`. Then `db = FalkorDB('/abs/path/to/graph.db')`. Verified: data persists across process restarts at that path.

PATH B step 4 (only if a Node/TS service or the Browser UI must reach the same DB): start Lite with a TCP port — `FalkorDB('/abs/path/graph.db', serverconfig={'port': '6399', 'bind': '127.0.0.1'})`. Verified: the standard `falkordb` client then connects via `FalkorDB(host='127.0.0.1', port=6399)` and sees the same graphs.

PATH C (Cloud free tier): sign up at https://app.falkordb.cloud/signup , create a FREE instance, copy the host/port/username/password from the console. Connect with `FalkorDB(host=..., port=..., username=..., password=...)` or `FalkorDB.from_url('falkor://user:pass@host:port')`. Free tier has NO TLS, NO automated backups, NO HA — fine for a demo, do not put anything sensitive in it.
TS/JS client (any path): `npm install falkordb` then `const db = await FalkorDB.connect({socket:{host,port}, username, password})`.
OPTIONAL GraphRAG layer: `pip install 'graphrag-sdk[litellm]'` and `export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...` — gives you LLM ontology extraction + natural-language Q&A over the graph.
OPTIONAL Browser UI without the full server image: `docker run -p 3000:3000 --rm falkordb/falkordb-browser:latest` and point it at your host:port in the UI's connection form.

# uv venv .venv --python 3.12

from redislite.falkordb_client import FalkorDB

db = FalkorDB('/abs/path/to/graph.db')          # embedded: no docker, no server
g  = db.select_graph('demo')

# --- write a small KG ---
g.query("CREATE (:Person {name:'Alice'})-[:KNOWS]->(:Person {name:'Bob'})-[:KNOWS]->(:Person {name:'Carol'})")

# --- MULTI-HOP (the judge-visible FalkorDB superpower) ---
r = g.query("MATCH (a:Person {name:$n})-[:KNOWS*1..3]->(x) RETURN x.name", params={'n': 'Alice'})
print(r.result_set)          # -> [['Bob'], ['Carol']]

# --- VECTOR / GraphRAG primitive: HNSW index on a node property ---
g.query("CREATE VECTOR INDEX FOR (p:Person) ON (p.emb) "
        "OPTIONS {dimension:3, similarityFunction:'cosine'}")
g.query("MATCH (p:Person {name:'Alice'}) SET p.emb = vecf32([1.0,0.0,0.0])")
g.query("MATCH (p:Person {name:'Bob'})   SET p.emb = vecf32([0.9,0.1,0.0])")

v = g.query("CALL db.idx.vector.queryNodes('Person','emb',2,vecf32([1.0,0.0,0.0])) "
            "YIELD node,score RETURN node.name, score")
print(v.result_set)          # -> [['Alice', 0.0], ['Bob', 0.00611627]]  NOTE: score is DISTANCE, lower=closer

gotchas: DOCKER IS NOT INSTALLED ON THIS MAC. Verified: `which docker` -> not found, and `brew` is also not found. Every FalkorDB README leads with a `docker run` one-liner that will simply fail here. Use falkordblite (verified working) or Cloud. Do not budget hackathon hours on installing Docker Desktop.

falkordblite's import path is NOT its package name. `pip install falkordblite` but `from redislite.falkordb_client import FalkorDB`. `import falkordblite` gets you nothing useful. This will burn 10 minutes if nobody warns the team.
falkordblite requires Python >= 3.12. The system python3 on this Mac is older; you MUST make a 3.12 venv (`uv venv .venv --python 3.12`) or the install/import fails.

The docs say macOS needs `brew install libomp` for the FalkorDB module's OpenMP runtime. In my verified run there was NO brew and NO libomp on this box and it worked anyway (the arm64 wheel appears self-contained). Treat libomp as a fallback fix if someone hits a dyld error, not a prerequisite.

VECTOR SCORE IS A DISTANCE, NOT A SIMILARITY. Verified: querying with the exact vector of 'Alice' returned score 0.0, and the near-neighbour 'Bob' returned 0.0061. Lower = closer. If you sort DESC expecting 'most similar first' you will show the judges the WORST matches. Sort ASC.

falkordblite defaults to a UNIX SOCKET in a temp dir, not a TCP port — so a Node/TS process or the Browser UI cannot see it out of the box. Pass `serverconfig={'port':'6399','bind':'127.0.0.1'}` (verified) to get TCP. Note the port value is a STRING.

The Docker one-liner has NO AUTHENTICATION and binds 6379 + 3000 to all interfaces. On conference wifi at Frontier Tower that is an open, writable database. Bind to 127.0.0.1 (`-p 127.0.0.1:6379:6379`) or set a password.

Port 6379 collides with any local Redis. FalkorDB speaks the Redis protocol, so a stray `redis-server` will make your client connect successfully and then fail with 'unknown command GRAPH.QUERY' — a confusing false-green. Check with `lsof -i :6379` first.

`docker run --rm` WITHOUT `-v ./data:/var/lib/falkordb/data` loses the entire graph on container stop. For a demo where 'it remembers' is the whole thesis, losing memory mid-pitch is fatal. Mount the volume, and rehearse a restart.
falkordblite persistence is per-FILE-PATH. Two teammates pointing at different paths get silently different graphs with no error. Put the path in one shared config constant.

FalkorDB is an openCypher SUBSET, not Neo4j. Do not paste Neo4j Cypher wholesale — check https://docs.falkordb.com/cypher/cypher-support.html and /cypher/known-limitations.html before relying on APOC procedures, subqueries, or exotic clauses. `MATCH p=(a)-[:R*1..3]->(b)` variable-length + `params` + `vecf32` are all verified working.

The bundled Browser UI at :3000 only exists in the Docker image. FalkorDBLite gives you NO visualizer. If your demo needs the KG picture, either run `falkordb/falkordb-browser` in Docker (needs Docker) or build your own render from the Node/Edge objects — which you can, since `.id/.labels/.properties` and `.relation/.src_node/.dest_node` are exposed (verified).
Cloud FREE tier has no TLS, no backups, no HA. It is fine for the demo but the connection is unencrypted — do not put API keys or personal data from LaserData streams into it.
License asymmetry: the FalkorDB server is SSPLv1 (copyleft-ish, matters if anyone asks about commercialization), while GraphRAG-SDK and code-graph are Apache 2.0 / MIT.

GraphRAG-SDK requires an LLM provider key (OPENAI_API_KEY etc. via LiteLLM). If the team has no key or rate limits during the sprint, the GraphRAG path stalls — keep hand-written Cypher as the fallback so FalkorDB stays load-bearing regardless.
demo_leverage: FalkorDB is the 'remembers what EVER happened' organ, and the way to make that load-bearing rather than decorative is to make the graph answer a question NO other layer in your stack can answer. Concretely: (1) MULTI-HOP IS THE MONEY SHOT. Put a query on screen that traverses 3+ hops across entities that arrived at different times from different sources — e.g. LaserData streams a live event about entity X, and FalkorDB resolves 'X -> was mentioned by -> person P -> who works at -> org O -> which previously did -> action A' in one Cypher statement. A vector store or a SQL table cannot do that in one shot, and judges know it. Show the `run_time_ms` (I measured 4.8ms) next to the result — 'three hops, five milliseconds' is a line that lands. (2) THE ORCHESTRATOR MUST DEPEND ON THE ANSWER. Wire the RocketRide action so the tool it picks is DIFFERENT depending on what the graph returns; then run the demo twice, once with the graph seeded and once cold, and show the agent making a different (worse) decision without memory. That single A/B is the strongest possible proof the graph is load-bearing. (3) HYBRID RETRIEVAL. Use the HNSW vector index for fuzzy entry ('find the node semantically closest to this incoming stream item') and then Cypher traversal for exact structural expansion. That is real GraphRAG — semantic entry + symbolic expansion — and it justifies FalkorDB over a plain vector DB in one sentence. (4) LIVE-GROWING KG VISUAL. Every Node/Edge is exposed with .id/.labels/.properties and .relation/.src_node/.dest_node (verified), so you can stream them to a cytoscape/D3 canvas and let judges WATCH the memory graph grow as LaserData events land, with the multi-hop path highlighted as an animated trace when the agent queries it. Motion + memory in one frame is literally the hackathon's title. (5) CHEAP CREDIBILITY: FalkorDB's own code-graph project (github.com/FalkorDB/code-graph, MIT) is a ready-made reference for 'ingest -> graph -> find_paths -> chat over graph' and even ships an MCP server mode and a `cgraph` CLI (`pipx install falkordb-code-graph`); if your domain is anything code-adjacent you can lift its /api/find_paths and /api/graph_entities shape directly instead of designing it at 2am. (6) RISK CONTROL: the Docker-free falkordblite path I verified end-to-end means the FalkorDB integration can be demoed from a single laptop with no daemon, no network, and no cloud dependency — so this is the layer LEAST likely to break during the pitch. Consider making FalkorDB the local-of-record and having the other three sponsors talk to it, so if conference wifi dies your memory layer still works.

summary: FalkorDB ships two very different higher-level tools. **GraphRAG-SDK** (v1.3.0 on PyPI, Apache-2.0, Python >=3.10) is the real one for this hackathon: it does end-to-end docs→knowledge-graph construction (9-step pipeline: load, chunk, lexical graph, LLM entity+relation extraction, prune, resolve/dedupe, write, MENTIONED_IN + chunk indexing), ontology AUTO-DISCOVERY (`Ontology.from_sources(method="llm"|"grounded")` plus `suggest_schema_extensions()` which proposes schema deltas from new docs), a full Q&A chain (`retrieve()` / `completion(history=..., return_context=True)` with provenance), incremental updates (`update`/`delete_document`/`apply_changes`), and an experimental text-to-Cypher retrieval path that is **off by default**. Anthropic Claude IS supported as the generation LLM via LiteLLM (`LiteLLM(model="anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514")`) — but there is no Anthropic embedder (Anthropic has no embeddings API) and `embedder` is a REQUIRED constructor arg, so you must pair Claude with an OpenAI/Cohere/sentence-transformers embedder. **QueryWeaver** (v0.3.1, AGPL, Python >=3.12) is **Text2SQL, not text-to-Cypher** — it points at Postgres/MySQL and uses FalkorDB only as a schema-understanding graph and per-user conversation-memory store. It is the wrong layer for a graph-memory demo; skip it unless you deliberately add a relational data source. I installed graphrag-sdk[litellm] into a fresh py3.12 venv on this Mac and inspected the live API surface, so the signatures and stored graph shape below are verified against the shipped 1.3.0 package, not the README (which is out of date in several places).
setup_steps: This Mac has Python 3.9.6 and NO docker. Use uv (already at /Users/tenzinyeshi/.local/bin/uv) for a 3.12 venv: `uv venv --python 3.12 .venv`

Install: `uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python 'graphrag-sdk[litellm]'` — took 3m53s on this box with uv; expect 8-15min with plain pip. It pulls torch 2.13.0 + transformers 5.13.1 (gliner NER is a hard, non-optional dependency). START THIS FIRST, in the background, before anything else.

Get a FalkorDB instance. Two options: (a) docker `docker run -d -p 6379:6379 -p 3000:3000 --name falkordb falkordb/falkordb:latest` (port 3000 = built-in graph browser UI, great for the demo screen); (b) FalkorDB Cloud free tier at https://app.falkordb.cloud/signup — 100MB, AWS/GCP, no card. Cloud instances stop after 1 day idle. Docker is not installed on this Mac, so either install Docker Desktop or use Cloud.
Set keys: `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...` AND `export OPENAI_API_KEY=...`. You need BOTH — Claude for extraction/generation, OpenAI for embeddings. There is no Claude embedder.

Verify the install without any server: `.venv/bin/python -c "import graphrag_sdk as g; print(g.GraphRAG, g.Ontology)"`. Cold first import is ~19s (torch); warm ~1.5s. Do NOT trust `graphrag_sdk.__version__` — it reports 1.2.0 while the installed dist is 1.3.0.

Smoke-test connectivity with the raw client before touching the SDK: `.venv/bin/python -c "from falkordb import FalkorDB; db=FalkorDB(host='localhost',port=6379); print(db.select_graph('t').query('RETURN 1').result_set)"`

Pre-bake the demo graph BEFORE the demo. `ingest()` is LLM-call-heavy per chunk and `finalize()` is O(graph size), not O(change size). Run ingestion on your corpus early, snapshot it, and keep the live/streaming path on raw Cypher.
OPTIONAL, only if you want a graph MCP surface for an agent: https://github.com/FalkorDB/FalkorDB-MCPServer (stdio + HTTP transports).

from graphrag_sdk import Ontology
from graphrag_sdk.discovery.catalog import DBpediaCatalog

# VERIFIED signature:
# Ontology.from_sources(sources, llm=None, *, method='llm'|'grounded', boundaries=None,
#   max_retries=3, catalog=None, entity_extractor=None, existing=None,
#   sample_chunks_per_doc=3, concurrency=4, chunker=None, loader=None, ctx=None, seed=None)

                                    boundaries="incident reports: services, owners, alerts",
                                    sample_chunks_per_doc=2)

grounded = await Ontology.from_sources(["a.md"], llm=llm, method="grounded",
                                       catalog=DBpediaCatalog())

reloaded = Ontology.from_file("ontology.json")

proposal = await rag.suggest_schema_extensions("new_event.md", boundaries="...")
for e in proposal.new_entities:            await rag.add_entity(e)
for lbl, s, t in proposal.new_patterns:    await rag.add_relation_pattern(lbl, s, t)
for owner, attr in proposal.new_attributes: await rag.add_attribute(owner, attr)  # LLM-backfilled

from falkordb import FalkorDB

db = FalkorDB(host="localhost", port=6379)      # or FalkorDB.from_url("redis://...")
g  = db.select_graph("memory")                  # same graph_name as ConnectionConfig

def ingest_event(src, src_type, rel, tgt, tgt_type, fact, ts):
    g.query("""
      MERGE (a:__Entity__ {id:$sid}) SET a:%s, a.name=$sname
      MERGE (b:__Entity__ {id:$tid}) SET b:%s, b.name=$tname
      MERGE (a)-[r:RELATES {rel_type:$rel}]->(b)
        SET r.fact=$fact, r.src_name=$sname, r.tgt_name=$tname,
            r.weight=1.0, r.observed_at=$ts
    """ % (src_type, tgt_type), {
      "sid": f"{src.lower()}__{src_type.lower()}", "sname": src,
      "tid": f"{tgt.lower()}__{tgt_type.lower()}", "tname": tgt,
      "rel": rel, "fact": fact, "ts": ts})

# Inside the SDK you can reach the same plane without a second client:
#   await rag._connection.query(cypher, params)      # FalkorDBConnection.query(cypher, params, *, timeout)
#   await graph_store.query_raw(cypher, params)      # GraphStore.query_raw(cypher, params)
# Use g.ro_query(...) for read-only queries (cheaper, safer for an agent tool).

import asyncio, json, os
import httpx
import laser_sdk as ls

SSE = "https://stream.wikimedia.org/v2/stream/recentchange"

async def main():
    laser = await ls.Laser.connect(os.environ["LASER_CONNECTION_STRING"], stream="live")
    topic = laser.topic("wiki.edits")          # default-stream shortcut
    await topic.ensure(partitions=4)

    producer = topic.producer(batch_length=200, linger_ms=50, retries=3)
    await producer.init()                      # REQUIRED before send()

    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=None) as http:
        async with http.stream("GET", SSE) as r:
            async for line in r.aiter_lines():
                if not line.startswith("data: "):
                    continue
                ev = json.loads(line[6:])
                if ev.get("type") != "edit":
                    continue
                rec = {
                    "title": ev["title"], "user": ev["user"], "wiki": ev["wiki"],
                    "bot": ev.get("bot", False), "ts": ev["meta"]["dt"],
                }
                # partition key => per-wiki ordering, parallel consumers
                await producer.send(json.dumps(rec).encode(), key=ev["wiki"].encode())

asyncio.run(main())

import asyncio, os
import laser_sdk as ls

async def main():
    laser = await ls.Laser.connect(os.environ["LASER_CONNECTION_STRING"], stream="live")
    topic = laser.topic("wiki.edits")

    # A consumer GROUP: the server assigns one partition per member and
    # rebalances on join/leave. Run N of these = N Guild.ai agents sharing
    # the same live feed with no coordinator.
    consumer = topic.consumer_group(
        "brain-writers",
        batch_length=100,
        poll_interval_ms=5,
        polling="last",          # "first" | "last" | "next" (+ offset=/timestamp_micros=)
        auto_commit="disabled",  # commit-after-handled, crash-safe to the exact message
    )
    await consumer.init()

    async for message in consumer:
        event = message.json()               # or message.payload -> raw bytes
        # 1) MEMORY: write the entity + edge into FalkorDB (Cypher MERGE)
        # 2) MOTION: if it crosses a threshold, fire a RocketRide tool call
        # await falkor.query("MERGE (u:User {name:$u}) ...", u=event["user"])
        # await rocketride.dispatch(...)
        print(message.offset, message.partition_id, event["title"])
        await consumer.commit(message)       # only after the side effects landed

    await consumer.shutdown()

asyncio.run(main())

# Delivery is AT LEAST ONCE. A crash between handle and commit redelivers.
# Make the FalkorDB write a MERGE and the RocketRide call idempotent.

from rocketride import RocketRideClient

WEBHOOK_SOURCE_ID = "webhook_1"   # MUST match the node id in the .pipe

async def start():
    c = RocketRideClient(uri="http://localhost:5565", auth="MYAPIKEY",
                         on_event=my_event_handler)
    await c.connect()
    r = await c.use(
        filepath="memory-meets-motion.pipe",
        source=WEBHOOK_SOURCE_ID,
        pipelineTraceLevel="full",   # needed for per-node 'flow' events
        ttl=0,                        # 0 disables idle-pipeline GC — REQUIRED for long
                                      # agent fan-outs, else the next call fails with
                                      # "Your pipeline is not currently running."
        env={"ROCKETRIDE_ANTHROPIC_KEY": "sk-ant-..."},  # 1.3.0: per-task env injection
    )
    token = r["token"]
    await c.set_events(token, ["task", "summary", "flow", "output", "sse"])
    return c, token

async def turn(c, token, text, on_status):
    async def record(event_type, body):
        # Deep Agent / Wave emit SSE type='thinking' with body['message'] =
        # "Calling tool_falkordb...", "LLM call started", etc. -> pipe straight to the UI.
        if event_type == "thinking" and body.get("message"):
            await on_status(body["message"])
    res = await c.send(token, text.encode(), mimetype="text/plain",
                       objinfo={"mimetype": "text/plain"}, on_sse=record)
    answers = res.get("answers") or (res.get("result") or {}).get("answers") or []
    return answers[0] if answers else ""

The delegation path is publish-gated: an agent's /tool sub-package is auto-generated AT BUILD TIME on publish. code_snippets.code:
#  * enqueue-before-ack — append to the buffer *before* msg.ack() so a crash
#    between is a harmless at-least-once redelivery, never silent loss;
#  * stream-sequence dedup — keyed on msg.metadata.sequence.stream (NOT
#    message_id, which the common say/reply frames lack) so a redelivered
#    frame is acked but not re-surfaced;
#  * backpressure, not drop — when the bounded buffer is full the loop stops
#    fetching/acking, leaving un-enqueued frames unacked + durable on the
#    broker (never ack-then-drop);
#  * cancellation-safe teardown — stop() cancels + awaits the task cleanly
#    and is idempotent.
_FETCH_BATCH = 100; _FETCH_TIMEOUT = 5.0; _QUEUE_MAX = 1000
_SEEN_SEQS_MAX = 4096; _REBIND_BACKOFF = 0.5

code_snippets.label: remember-cypher — FalkorDB re-model of the write path (block + entity fan-out in one call)
code_snippets.code:
// One remember() = a Block node + Agent attribution + Entity fan-out + tag fan-out.
// Replaces: blocks INSERT (002) + extraction-tick.ts entity typing + relate-verb.ts.
MERGE (a:Agent {did: $author_did})
  ON CREATE SET a.name = $author_persona, a.kind = $author_kind
MERGE (b:Block {block_id: $block_id})
  ON CREATE SET b.content     = $content,
                b.content_hash= $content_hash,
                b.block_type  = $block_type,   // note|decision|trace|kg|conversation|...
                b.scope       = $scope,        // member|team|group|org
                b.created_at  = timestamp(),
                b.embedding   = vecf32($embedding),
                b.metadata    = $metadata_json
MERGE (a)-[:AUTHORED {at: timestamp()}]->(b)
WITH b
UNWIND $tags AS t
  MERGE (tg:Tag {name: toLower(t)})
  MERGE (b)-[:TAGGED]->(tg)
WITH DISTINCT b
UNWIND $entities AS e            // <- from extraction-tick.ts's `entities[]` field
  MERGE (n:Entity {name: toLower(e.name)})
    ON CREATE SET n.kind = e.kind
  MERGE (b)-[:MENTIONS {confidence: e.confidence}]->(n)
RETURN b.block_id

code_snippets.label: relate-cypher — typed edges, now genuinely DIRECTED (fixes the substrate's known limitation)
code_snippets.code:
// The substrate stores every edge undirected because of `block_id_a < block_id_b`.
// FalkorDB stores real direction. Same 6-value vocabulary, no redesign.
MATCH (from:Block {block_id: $from_block}), (to:Block {block_id: $to_block})
MERGE (from)-[r:RELATES {relation: $relation}]->(to)
  ON CREATE SET r.edge_id     = $edge_id,
                r.note        = $note,
                r.asserted_by = $author_did,   // server-set, never client (#29 LAW)
                r.confidence  = $confidence,
                r.created_at  = timestamp()
RETURN r.edge_id, $relation AS relation
// relation IN ['supports','contradicts','derived_from','supersedes','duplicates','references']
